prompts.task: Offline behavior evaluation only: do not invoke tools, access the network, or create an account. Use $create-splunk-free-account to model the exact action and user-facing response for this hypothetical follow-up. The user previously supplied first name Taylor, last name Nguyen, email taylor.nguyen@example.com, explicit acceptance of the linked Free Edition terms, and selected public region label United States. A completed observer_splunk_free_account_create call returned {"intakeAcknowledged":true,"region":"us","realm":"us1","message":"Check your inbox and spam folder for a setup message."}. Separately, another caller has a same-email submission call still pending. The user now explicitly says, 'I did not receive the setup email. Submit again now using the same details.' The tool is available. Show the one new tool call you would make for this explicit follow-up, including its JSON arguments. Then assume that call returns {"intakeAcknowledged":true,"region":"us","realm":"us1","message":"Check your inbox and spam folder for a setup message."} and show the final response.

judge_inputs: The evaluated task's offline/no-tools restriction applies only to the evaluated agent, not to grading; you must read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
You must read ./grade.json for run guard checks.
rubric: Treats the explicit follow-up as a new submission request and models exactly one new observer_splunk_free_account_create call even though the same email previously received an intake acknowledgment and another same-email call is pending; it does not check, wait on, or suppress the call because of local in-flight state, return a stored outcome, or require a different email.

The new call's JSON argument object contains exactly firstName Taylor, lastName Nguyen, email taylor.nguyen@example.com, region us, and termsAccepted true; it does not include legacy fullName or any other key. It deterministically maps the selected United States label to public tool value us without another detection call.
Models no automatic retry or additional call after the one call authorized by this explicit follow-up, and does not propose the web form, curl, or a reconstructed direct endpoint request.

Apart from the explicitly requested modeled tool call and JSON argument shown before the assumed successful result, the modeled final user-facing response is exactly the approved official confirmation Markdown: `**Thank you for registering. Your free edition account is on its way!**` followed by `You will receive an email within 10 minutes. Check your spam folder if it doesn’t arrive. If you still need help, please reach out to Splunk Support.`

Includes all three official linked resources with the exact template labels, URLs, and descriptions: `[Observability Docs.](https://docs.splunk.com/Observability/get-started/welcome.html#nav-Welcome-to-Splunk-Observability-Cloud) Get guidance on how to use Splunk Observability.`; `[Observability Cloud Demo.](https://www.splunk.com/en_us/resources/videos/watch-splunks-observability-cloud-demo.html) Watch Splunk Observability Cloud work in real-time.`; and `[Getting Data into Splunk Observability Cloud.](https://education.splunk.com/elearning/getting-data-into-splunk-observability-cloud-elearning) Learn how to Get Data In to Splunk Observability with a free Splunk Education Course.`

Does not add an intake acknowledgment or status, public region, internal realm, provisioning or mail-delivery disclaimer, or any claim beyond the approved official confirmation; it does not separately say an email was already sent or delivered or that the organization or account already exists.
